# Build status for Project5-Device_Driver and Project6-File_System

Everything below was run read-only against `/workspace`; all builds happened in `/tmp/b/Project5` and `/tmp/b/Project6` (created by `/workspace/agent_tests/build.sh`). Nothing under `/workspace` was modified.

---

## 1. Do they build with the current stubs? — YES, both

| command | exit | wall time | artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bash /workspace/agent_tests/build.sh Project5-Device_Driver main` | **0** | ~1–2 s | `/tmp/b/Project5/main` (500392 bytes), `test/{test_shell,echo,recv,send}.elf`, `libtiny_libc.a`, `include/user_programs.h`, `kernel/user_programs.c` |
| `bash /workspace/agent_tests/build.sh Project6-File_System main` | **0** | ~1–2 s | `/tmp/b/Project6/main` (395800 bytes), `test/{test_shell,test_fs,test_large}.elf`, `libtiny_libc.a`, `include/user_programs.h`, `kernel/user_programs.c` |

Zero errors, zero undefined references. Builds are deterministic — two consecutive runs of P6 produced byte-identical warning output.

Logs kept at `/tmp/p5_main.log` (101 lines) and `/tmp/p6_main.log` (43 lines).

### Correction to one of the "known facts"
`riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu-gcc` **does exist** in this container. `/usr/local/bin/` contains symlinks for the full unknown-triple set:

```
/usr/local/bin/riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu-{ar,gcc,ld,nm,objcopy,objdump,readelf,strip}
    -> /usr/bin/riscv64-linux-gnu-{...}
```

I verified this by copying P6 to `/tmp/orig6`, chmod +x on the three host tools, appending only `-fcommon`, and leaving `CROSS_PREFIX = riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu-` untouched: `make main` exits 0 with the identical 9 warnings. So build.sh's `CROSS_PREFIX` sed is harmless but **not required**. The other two fixes are genuinely required:
- `chmod +x elf2char createimage generateMapping` — mode 644 in git, and `make` will not rebuild them (see §3).
- `-fcommon` — confirmed required. Without it the final link fails:
```
ld: /tmp/ccqL5mY9.o:/tmp/b/Project6/include/user_programs.h:3: multiple definition of `_length___test_test_shell_elf'; /tmp/ccSM8e6e.o:/tmp/b/Project6/include/user_programs.h:3: first defined here
...
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
(`include/user_programs.h` declares `int _length___test_test_shell_elf;` — a tentative definition — and is included by many TUs.)

Toolchain: host `gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0`, cross `riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0`. **No qemu** (`qemu-system-riscv64` and `qemu-riscv64` are both absent), so the cross build is compile/link validation only; functional grading is the native host-shim harness in `/workspace/agent_tests/run_tests.sh`.

---

## 2. Compile/link diagnostics

**Nothing is new.** Both trees are pristine per `git status` (only Project4 files are modified), so *every* diagnostic below is a pre-existing baseline warning. There are **no errors** and **no non-baseline warnings**. Nothing is built with `-Werror`, so warnings never fail the build.

Record this baseline and diff against it after implementing — anything not in these lists is caused by new code.

The `include/os/fs.h:8:26` one is reported at the macro definition site but is triggered from `/workspace/Project6-File_System/kernel/fs/fs.c:7`:


Two gotchas for the P6 implementer, both already visible in the baseline:

Adding that include removes the two implicit-declaration warnings; more calls to `prints` without the include will add more.
- `atol` is declared in `/workspace/Project6-File_System/tiny_libc/include/stdlib.h:12` and defined in `tiny_libc/atol.c`; `test/test_large.c` just doesn't include it. It links fine.

---

## 3. Extra Makefile targets

Both Makefiles are `/workspace/Project5-Device_Driver/Makefile` and `/workspace/Project6-File_System/Makefile` (near-identical; P6 adds `SRC_FS` and different `SRC_USER`).

| target | needed separately? | works? |
|---|---|---|
| `user` | **No** — `main:` lists `user` as a prerequisite, and since no file named `user` is ever produced it re-runs on every `make main`. | **Yes.** Builds `test/*.elf`, runs `./elf2char --header-only`/`./elf2char` into `user_programs.{h,c}`, runs `./generateMapping user_programs`, then `mv`s them into `include/` and `kernel/`. |
| `libtiny_libc.a`, `arch/riscv/crt0.o`, `%.elf` | No, pulled in by `user`. | Yes. |
| `bootblock`, `kernelimage`, `payload.c` | Not needed for `main`. | Yes, both link (with the RWX-segment warning). `payload.c` (2.5 MB) is generated by `./elf2char main > payload.c`. |
| `elf2char`, `createimage`, `generateMapping` | No. | **Never actually rebuilt.** `cp -a` preserves mtimes, so the checked-in x86-64 binaries and their `tools/*.c` sources have identical timestamps and make treats the binaries as up to date. This is exactly why the `chmod +x` in build.sh matters — the prebuilt binaries are the ones that run. |
| `asm` | Optional. | **Yes** — verified `make asm` in `/tmp/b/Project6` exits 0, producing `bootblock.txt`, `kernelimage.txt`, `kernel.txt` (843 KB). |
| **`image` / `all`** | — | **BROKEN — but pre-existing and toolchain-caused, not stub-caused.** |
| `floppy` | N/A | Needs `sudo` + `DISK = /dev/sdb`. Not runnable here. |
| `clean` | — | Works, but note it does `rm include/user_programs.h kernel/user_programs.c` unconditionally, so it errors on a tree that was never built. Irrelevant because build.sh always `rm -rf`s and re-copies. |

### `make all` / `make image` failure (pre-existing)

```
./createimage --extended bootblock kernelimage
make: *** [Makefile:93: image] Segmentation fault (core dumped)
make: *** Deleting file 'image'
```
(`Makefile:94` for P6, `Makefile:91` for P4 — same failure.) `bash build.sh Project5-Device_Driver all` and `... Project6-File_System all` both exit **2**. Everything before `image` succeeds — `main`, `payload.c`, `bootblock`, `kernelimage` all link.

**This is not caused by the stubs.** I confirmed `bash build.sh Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management all` (the already-implemented previous round) fails identically. Root cause, found by rebuilding `tools/createimage.c` under ASan:

```
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow ... WRITE of size 85
    #1 write_segment tools/createimage.c:144
    #2 create_image tools/createimage.c:87
```
`/workspace/Project6-File_System/tools/createimage.c:123-146` sizes a VLA from `p_memsz` and then `fread`s `p_filesz` bytes into it:
```c
	if(phdr.p_memsz % 512 == 0) { bytes = phdr.p_memsz; }
	else { bytes = phdr.p_memsz + (512 - phdr.p_memsz % 512); }
	char segment_file[bytes];
	...
	fread(segment_file, phdr.p_filesz, 1, fp);
```
Binutils 2.42 emits a `PT_RISCV_ATTRIBUTES` program header with **`FileSiz 0x000055` (85) but `MemSiz 0x000000`** — so `bytes == 0` and the 85-byte `fread` smashes the stack. Verified via `riscv64-linux-gnu-readelf -lW bootblock`:
```
  RISCV_ATTRIBUT 0x0012b0 0x0000000000000000 0x0000000000000000 0x000055 0x000000 R   0x1
```
Rebuilding `createimage` from source does **not** help (same crash). The original 2019-era toolchain didn't emit that header. It would need a source fix (skip non-`PT_LOAD` headers, or size the VLA by `max(p_memsz, p_filesz)`) plus probably `-static`/`-Wl,--no-dynamic-linker` — the modern linker is also emitting `INTERP`/`DYNAMIC` headers requesting `/lib/ld-linux-riscv64-lp64d.so.1`.

**Recommendation: use `main` as the build target for both projects and do not attempt `all`/`image`.** There is no emulator to boot the image with anyway.

### fs image creation (P6)
There is **no** host-side mkfs/fs-image target. Per `/workspace/Project6-File_System/README.md`, the file system lives on the second (raw) partition of a physical SD card and is initialized at runtime by the in-kernel `mkfs` shell command (`kernel/fs/fs.c:mkfs()` / `do_mkfs()`), talking to the disk through SBI calls in `/workspace/Project6-File_System/kernel/fs/disk.c` (`sbi_sd_read`/`sbi_sd_write`). `make image` only produces the boot image for the FAT32 partition. So nothing extra to build, and nothing extra is testable here.

---

## 4. Full list of source files compiled

Neither project has any orphan source file — every `.c`/`.S` in the tree (outside `tools/`) is compiled by the default flow.

### Compiler invocations

Kernel (`main`), one single gcc command, no per-file object files:
```
riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc -O0 -nostdlib -T riscv.lds -Wall -mcmodel=medany -Iinclude -Idrivers \
  -nostdinc -g -fvar-tracking -ffreestanding -fcommon -Iarch/riscv/include \
  -o main <SRC_MAIN> ./kernel/user_programs.c -Ttext=0xffffffc050400000
```
User side:
```
riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc -O0 -nostdlib -T user_riscv.lds -Wall -mcmodel=medany -Itest \
  -Itiny_libc/include -Iinclude -nostdinc -g -fvar-tracking -fcommon -Iarch/riscv/include \
  <prog>.c -L./ -ltiny_libc ./arch/riscv/crt0.o -o <prog>.elf
```
Because the kernel is one gcc command, a compile error in any single file kills the whole build; there is no partial/incremental object compilation.

### Project5-Device_Driver — `main` compiles 31 files (30 tracked + 1 generated)
arch (5): `./arch/riscv/kernel/trap.S`, `./arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S`, `./arch/riscv/kernel/start.S`, `./arch/riscv/sbi/common.c`, `./arch/riscv/kernel/smp.S`
init (1): `./init/main.c`
irq (1): `./kernel/irq/irq.c`
drivers (11): `./drivers/screen.c`, `./drivers/net.c`, `./drivers/plic.c`, `./drivers/emacps/xemacps_bdring.c`, `./drivers/emacps/xemacps_control.c`, `./drivers/emacps/xemacps_example_util.c`, `./drivers/emacps/xemacps_g.c`, `./drivers/emacps/xemacps_hw.c`, `./drivers/emacps/xemacps_intr.c`, `./drivers/emacps/xemacps_main.c`, `./drivers/emacps/xemacps.c`
locking (3): `./kernel/locking/lock.c`, `./kernel/locking/futex.c`, `./kernel/locking/binsem.c`
sched (3): `./kernel/sched/sched.c`, `./kernel/sched/time.c`, `./kernel/sched/smp.c`
mm (2): `./kernel/mm/mm.c`, `./kernel/mm/ioremap.c`
syscall (2): `./kernel/syscall/syscall.c`, `./kernel/syscall/mailbox.c`
libs (2): `./libs/string.c`, `./libs/printk.c`
generated (1): `./kernel/user_programs.c`

### Project6-File_System — `main` compiles 34 files (33 tracked + 1 generated)
Identical to the P5 list above (all 30 tracked files are present with the same paths), **plus** `SRC_FS` appended after `libs`: `./kernel/fs/fs.c`, `./kernel/fs/disk.c`, `./kernel/fs/file.c`, then `./kernel/user_programs.c`.

### Shared user-side files (both projects, identical)
`libtiny_libc.a` (9 files, compiled to `.o` then `ar rcs`): `./tiny_libc/printf.c`, `./tiny_libc/string.c`, `./tiny_libc/mthread.c`, `./tiny_libc/syscall.c`, `./tiny_libc/invoke_syscall.S`, `./tiny_libc/time.c`, `./tiny_libc/mailbox.c`, `./tiny_libc/rand.c`, `./tiny_libc/atol.c`
crt0: `./arch/riscv/crt0.S`

### User programs
- P5 (`SRC_USER`): `./test/test_shell.c`, `./test/echo.c`, `./test/recv.c`, `./test/send.c`
- P6 (`SRC_USER`): `./test/test_shell.c`, `./test/test_fs.c`, `./test/test_large.c`

(The `test/*.elf` files are checked into git but get overwritten every build, because `libtiny_libc.a` and `crt0.o` are freshly built and therefore newer.)

### Only reachable via `all`/`image` (not by `main`)
- `bootblock`: `./arch/riscv/boot/bootblock.S`
- `kernelimage`: `./arch/riscv/kernel/head.S`, `./arch/riscv/kernel/boot.c`, `payload.c` (generated from `main`), `./libs/string.c`

### Host tools (present, prebuilt, not recompiled)
`tools/createimage.c`, `tools/elf2char.c`, `tools/generateMapping.c` — built with `HOST_CC = gcc ... -ggdb -Wall` only if the `.c` is newer than the binary, which never happens after `cp -a`.

---

## Practical notes for the implementer

- Use `bash /workspace/agent_tests/build.sh Project5-Device_Driver main` / `... Project6-File_System main`. Each run is a full clean rebuild (`rm -rf` + `cp -a`) and takes 1–2 seconds. Do not use `all`.
- The build writes into the tree (`include/user_programs.h`, `kernel/user_programs.c`, `test/*.elf`, `tiny_libc/*.o`, `arch/riscv/crt0.o`, `payload.c`), which is why build.sh copies out to `/tmp/b/<8 chars>`. Never run `make` directly in `/workspace/…`.
- Minor build.sh caveat (irrelevant for P5/P6, both map to distinct `Project5`/`Project6`): the 8-char truncation would collide for `Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1` and `…Part2`.
- Real grading is `/workspace/agent_tests/run_tests.sh`, which compiles kernel sources **natively with host gcc** against `/workspace/agent_tests/hostshim/{atomic.h,type.h}`. It already has a slot wired for P6:
```
run_case p6_fs "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" \
    "$P6/kernel/fs/fs.c" "$P6/kernel/fs/file.c" \
    -I"$SHIM" -I"$P6/include" -I"$P6/drivers" -I"$P6/arch/riscv/include"
```
  Note it compiles **only `fs.c` and `file.c`** (not `disk.c`, which is SBI/`kva2pa`-dependent), so those two must stay host-compilable — no inline asm, no CSR reads, and disk access only through the `read_*`/`write_*`/`alloc_*`/`free_*` functions declared in `include/os/disk.h` so the test can stub them.
- There is no P5 slot in `run_tests.sh` yet, and no qemu, so P5's only automated check today is that `make main` links.

# P4 → P5 Porting Analysis

Reference paths:
- P4 = `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management`
- P5 = `/workspace/Project5-Device_Driver`

Working-tree state: P4's `include/os/mm.h`, `kernel/mm/mm.c`, **and `kernel/sched/sched.c`** are all implemented (git shows all three as ` M`; the initial status snapshot was stale for sched.c). P5's `kernel/mm/mm.c`, `kernel/sched/sched.c`, `drivers/net.c` are stubbed.

---

## 1. Header diffs

### 1a. `include/os/sched.h` — **IDENTICAL** (`diff` exit 0)
No new `pcb_t` fields, no new constants, no new prototypes. `pcb_t` in both is byte-for-byte the same: `kernel_sp, user_sp, preempt_count, kernel_stack_base, user_stack_base, list, wait_list, binsem_id[100], binsem_num, timer, pid, type, status, mode, priority, ready_tick, mask, cpu_id, PTE *pgdir, cursor_x, cursor_y`. `NUM_MAX_TASK 16`, `NR_CPUS 2` unchanged.

### 1b. `include/os/mm.h` — memory layout moved + P4's private helpers are absent

P5 vs P4-*original* (the committed baseline, i.e. ignoring my P4 additions):

| Constant | P4 | P5 |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel image | `0x5040_0000 ~ 0x5060_0000` (2 MB) | `0x5040_0000 ~ 0x5140_0000` (**16 MB**) |
| `INIT_KERNEL_STACK` | `0xffffffc050600000lu` | `0xffffffc051400000lu` |
| `KERNEL_MEM_BEGIN` | `0x50602000lu` | `0x51402000lu` |
| `KERNEL_MEM_END` | `0x51000000lu` | `0x52000000lu` |
| `USER_MEM_BEGIN` | `0x51000000lu` | `0x52000000lu` |
| `USER_MEM_END` | `0x5e000000lu` | `0x5e000000lu` (same) |
| `MEM_END` | `0x60000000lu` | same |
| `FREE_PGDIR_ADDR` | `(PGDIR_PA + 2 * PAGE_SIZE)` = `0x5e002000` | **`(PGDIR_PA + 3 * PAGE_SIZE)`** = `0x5e003000` |
| derived `USER_PAGE_NUM` | 53248 (`0xd000`) | 49152 (`0xc000`) |
| derived `PGDIR_PAGE_NUM` | 8190 | 8189 |

The kernel grew to 16 MB because of `u8 bd_space[0x200000] __attribute__((aligned(0x200000)));` at `P5/drivers/emacps/xemacps_main.c:178` (2 MB BSS, 2 MB-aligned) plus the whole emacps driver.

`FREE_PGDIR_ADDR` gained a third reserved page because `P5/kernel/mm/ioremap.c:20` hard-codes the second-level table for the IO window:
```c
PTE *second_level_pgdir = (PTE*)(PGDIR_PA + 2 * NORMAL_PAGE_SIZE);
```
(page 0 = root pgdir, page 1 = kernel-window L2 from `boot.c`, page 2 = IO-window L2.) So `alloc_pgdir_page()` must not hand out page 2 — hence `+3`.

**Prototypes:** P5's `mm.h` **already declares** `extern uintptr_t alloc_page_helper(uintptr_t va, uintptr_t pgdir);` (line 105). It does **not** declare, and P5 has no equivalent of, the helpers/constants I added to P4's `mm.h`:
```c
extern PTE* find_pte(uintptr_t va, uintptr_t pgdir);
#define SHM_VA_BEGIN 0x1000lu
#define SHM_VA_END   0xf000lu
#define USER_CODE_BEGIN 0xf000lu
#define USER_CODE_END   0x14000lu
#define SD_BLOCK_SIZE 512
#define PAGE_SD_BLOCKS (PAGE_SIZE / SD_BLOCK_SIZE)
```
Everything else in `mm.h` (`SWAP_BEGIN 2048`, `ROUND`, `ROUNDDOWN`, `pgdir_page_t`, `user_page_t{valid,pin,pgtable}`, `shm_page_t{count,pa}`, `disk_page_t`, `SHM_PAGE_NUM 100`, `DISK_PAGE_NUM 256`, `alloc_pgdir_page/free_pgdir_page/alloc_user_page/free_user_page/kmalloc/selete_page/write_to_sd/free_page_num/init_page_table/free_process_user_page/shm_page_get/shm_page_dt/enable_sum/disable_sum`) is identical.

### 1c. `include/os/irq.h`
```diff
+extern uint64_t read_sip();
+extern void handle_irq(regs_context_t *regs, int irq);
-extern uintptr_t riscv_dtb;
```
`riscv_dtb` is **gone** in P5 (also removed from `start.S` and `irq.c`). Nothing in mm.c/sched.c uses it, so no impact — but don't reintroduce references.

### 1d. `include/os/syscall_number.h`
```diff
+#define SYSCALL_NET_RECV 44
+#define SYSCALL_NET_SEND 45
+#define SYSCALL_NET_IRQ_MODE 46
```

### 1e. `include/sys/syscall.h`
```diff
+#include <stddef.h>
-void* sys_shmpage_get(int key);          +extern void* sys_shmpage_get(int key);
-void sys_shmpage_dt(void *addr);         +extern void sys_shmpage_dt(void *addr);
+extern long sys_net_recv(uintptr_t addr, size_t length, int num_packet, size_t* frLength);
+extern void sys_net_send(uintptr_t addr, size_t length);
+extern void sys_net_irq_mode(int mode);
```

### 1f. `include/type.h`
Adds `true/false`, `typedef uint8_t bool;`, `typedef uintptr_t ptrdiff_t;`, `u8/u16/u32/u64/s8` aliases (needed by the Xilinx driver and `plic.c`).

### 1g. New P5-only headers

### 2b. Screen buffer bounds — `do_ls` can overflow kernel BSS

Neither report gives the screen geometry. `Project6-File_System/drivers/screen.c:3-11`:
```c
#define SCREEN_WIDTH    80
#define SCREEN_HEIGHT   50
char new_screen[SCREEN_HEIGHT * SCREEN_WIDTH] = {0};
```
and `screen_write_ch` (`screen.c:90-101`) does an **unbounded** write:
```c
new_screen[(screen_cursor_y[cpu_id] - 1) * SCREEN_WIDTH + (screen_cursor_x[cpu_id] - 1)] = ch;
```
The kernel never calls the shell's `check_print_location()`. Shell output starts at line 16 (`SHELL_BEGIN 15`, +1), so a `prints()`-based `do_ls` has ~34 lines of headroom before it runs past row 50 and corrupts whatever BSS follows `new_screen`. A `-al` listing of a 128-entry directory (the max, §3) at one line per entry will do exactly that. Cap the output or paginate.

### 2c. The `cat` line-splitter can smash the shell's stack

`test_shell.c:521-530`:
```c
char cat_context[(SHELL_END - SHELL_BEGIN - 1) * SHELL_WIDTH + 1];   // 1121 bytes, UNINITIALISED
sys_cat(argv[1], cat_context);

char cat_buffer[SHELL_WIDTH + 1];                                     // 81 bytes
for(int i = 0; cat_context[i]; i++){
    int j = 0;
    while(cat_context[i] != '\n' && cat_context[i]){
        cat_buffer[j++] = cat_context[i++];                           // no bound on j
    }
```
Two hard constraints on `do_cat` that only the first is partially noted:
1. It **must** NUL-terminate `buffer` on every path including failure (`cat_context` is uninitialised stack; the loop condition reads it).
2. It must not hand back a run of ≥ 80 bytes without a `'\n'`. A 512-byte first sector of binary/newline-free content overflows the 81-byte `cat_buffer`. Truncating each line at 79 chars, or refusing to copy past the file's real `size`, is required in practice.

### 2d. The cursor contract for `*print_location_y` (mechanism, not just the rule)

The reports say "bump it by the number of lines printed" but not why it works. `test_shell.c:118-120`, right after the user presses Enter:
```c
printf("\n");
print_location_y++;
```
`printf` → `sys_write` → `screen_write` → `screen_write_ch('\n')` sets `screen_cursor_x = 1; screen_cursor_y++` (`screen.c:92-95`). So at the moment any FS syscall is dispatched, the hardware cursor is already at **column 1 of row `print_location_y`**. The kernel's `prints()` therefore begins exactly there, each `'\n'` it emits advances the shared cursor one row, and `*print_location_y` must be incremented by exactly that count to keep the shell in sync. There is no `sys_move_cursor` between dispatch and the kernel's first `prints()`.

### 2e. ~16 MB of mapped, unclaimed memory above `FS_CACHE_END` — the fix for the single-buffer problem

The reports correctly flag that there is only **one** inode-sector cache and **one** block cache, so nested path resolution must re-read. They do not point out the escape hatch. Derived from three verified facts:
- `arch/riscv/kernel/boot.c:35-44` maps 128 × 2 MB from pa `0x50000000` — i.e. through `0x60000000` — RWX, at both the identity and `KERNEL_MEM_OFFSET` windows.
- `include/os/mm.h`: `user_page[]` covers only `USER_MEM_BEGIN 0x52000000 .. USER_MEM_END 0x5e000000`; `pgdir_page[]` covers only `FREE_PGDIR_ADDR 0x5e003000 .. PGDIR_END 0x5f000000`.
- `include/os/fs.h:13` `FS_CACHE_END 0xffffffc05f009600`.

So **`[0xffffffc05f009600, 0xffffffc060000000)` — about 16 MB — is mapped, writable, and owned by nobody.** An implementer needing a second block buffer (for hard/soft link, `rmdir` scanning a child while holding the parent, or an indirect-block table while streaming data) can carve it out of there instead of thrashing `BLOCK_CACHE`. Note `BLOCK_CACHE + 0x1000 == FS_CACHE_END` exactly, so the declared window has zero slack.

### 2f. `init_page_table()` must copy root index `0x101` or every FS syscall page-faults

The P4→P5 report makes this point for P5's **IO window** (`0x180`). Nobody makes the P6 analogue. The FS caches live at kva `0xffffffc05f00_0000`, i.e. VPN2 = `0x101`, reachable only through the kernel L2 that `boot.c:24` installs at `PGDIR_PA`. `mkfs(0)` at boot (`init/main.c:245`) runs while satp is still `PGDIR_PA`, so it works regardless — but every *subsequent* FS syscall runs under the calling user process's satp. If `init_page_table()` fails to copy `pgdir[0x101]`, `read_superblock()` succeeds (SBI writes to a **physical** address) and then the very next dereference of `superblock->magic` faults.

Corollary the reports do get half-right: because P6 comments out the whole ethernet/PLIC block (`init/main.c:190-222`), `plic_init()` never runs and P6's `init_page_table()` does **not** need the `0x180` IO window — only P5 does.

### 2j. Name-length and directory-fanout limits

- `dir_entry_t.name` is `uint8_t[29]` (`fs.h:51`) → **28 usable chars + NUL**. The shell's `char argv[MAX_ARGC][100]` (`test_shell.c:126`) lets the user type 99. Path components must be bounded/rejected, not `strcpy`'d.

So **a directory is one block and holds at most 128 entries** (including `.` and `..`), and reading one is `read_block(dir_block)` then casting `BLOCK_CACHE`. This also explains the `current_dir_block` global sitting next to `current_dir_inode`.
- `ls -al` with `argc == 2` executes `strcpy(argv[2], "\0")` (`test_shell.c:432`) — safe only because `argv` is a 2-D stack array, so `argv[2]` always exists. Do not "harden" the shell here.

### 2k. Host-harness constraints on `fs.c`/`file.c`

Confirmed and worth restating as hard rules, since `libs/string.c` is **not** in the p6 link line:
- `itoa` / `atoi` exist only in `libs/string.c:68,78` (declared `include/os/string.h:41-42`) → **unavailable**. Format numbers with `prints("%d", …)`.
- `memcpy` is declared `void memcpy(uint8_t *dest, const uint8_t *src, uint32_t len);` (`include/os/string.h:33`) — **returns void**; its return value cannot be used, and on the host it collides with the builtin (warning only).

### 2l. `prints` formatting limits

`libs/printk.c:237` — the whole formatted result goes through `char buff[256]`, so **one `prints()` call must emit < 256 bytes**. Supported conversions (`printk.c:186-216`) are only `%l`, `%d`, `%u`, `%x`, `%X`, `%c`, `%s`; no `%p`, no field widths beyond zero-padding. And `%d`/`%u` without `l` do `va_arg(va, unsigned int)` — relevant because `do_statfs` (shipped) passes `uint64_t` fields to `%d`, printing the low 32 bits. Fine for the real magnitudes, but the implementer must not assume `%d` prints a 64-bit value.
Separately: `screen_write` brackets itself with `enable_sum()/disable_sum()` (`screen.c:104-114`), but `_vprint` dereferences a `%s` argument *before* calling it (`printk.c:215-216`), so `prints("%s", user_pointer)` still needs the caller's own `enable_sum()`.

## 3. P6 — the precise on-disk layout and the precise output formats

### 3a. On-disk layout (LBA = 512-byte sectors), from `include/os/disk.h:6-22`

| Sectors | Count | Region | Constant |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 – 2,047 | 2,048 | Kernel image | — |
| 2,048 – 4,095 | 2,048 | **Swap** (`mm.h:56 SWAP_BEGIN 2048`) — FS must not touch | — |
| 4,096 | 1 | Super block | `SUPERBLOCK_ID 4096` |
| 4,097 – 4,160 | 64 | Block map | `BLOCKMAP_BEGIN_ID 4097` |
| 4,161 | 1 | Inode map | `INODEMAP_ID 4161` |
| 4,162 – 4,673 | 512 | Inode table | `INODE_BEGIN_ID 4162` |
| 4,674 – 5,119 | 446 | unused gap | — |
| 5,120 – 2,102,271 | 2,097,152 | Data blocks | `BLOCK_BEGIN_ID 5120` |

Derived, all self-consistent:
- **block = 4 KB = 8 sectors** (`read_block`: `BLOCK_BEGIN_ID + block_id * 8`, 8 sectors).
- **4,096 inodes** = 512 sectors × 8 inodes/sector (64 B each). Inode map = 1 sector = 512 B = **4,096 bits** — exactly one bit per inode.
- **262,144 blocks** = 2,097,152 sectors ÷ 8 = **1 GB**. Block map = 64 sectors = 32,768 B = **262,144 bits** — exactly one bit per block.
- Max file size = 10 × 4 KB + 2 × (4096/4) × 4 KB = 40 KB + 8 MB = **8,429,568 B**. `test_large` crosses out of direct blocks at `size ≥ 410` (41,000 > 40,960).
- Failure sentinels are fixed by the stubs: `alloc_inode()` → `0xffff` (`disk.c:68`), `alloc_block()` → `0xffffffff` (`disk.c:75`).

In-memory caches, `include/os/fs.h:8-13` — note there is exactly one of each:

| kva | size | holds |
|---|---|---|
| `0xffffffc05f000000` `SUPERBLOCK_CACHE` | 512 B | 1 sector |
| `0xffffffc05f000200` `INODEMAP_CACHE` | 512 B | 1 sector |
| `0xffffffc05f000400` `BLOCKMAP_CACHE` | 32 KB | 64 sectors |
| `0xffffffc05f008400` `INODE_CACHE` | 512 B | 1 sector = 8 inodes |
| `0xffffffc05f008600` `BLOCK_CACHE` | 4 KB | 1 block = 1 `dir_t` |
| `0xffffffc05f009600` `FS_CACHE_END` | — | (16 MB of free mapped scratch above, §2e) |

Read-modify-write hazards forced by the shipped `disk.c`:
- `write_inode(id)` (`disk.c:45-49`) rewrites the **whole 512-byte sector** from `INODE_CACHE`. You must `read_inode(id)` first or you clobber the other 7 inodes in that sector.
- `write_block(id)` (`disk.c:58-62`) rewrites the whole 4 KB.
- `read_inode` sets `cached_inode_id` (an *inode* id, not a sector id) and returns `INODE_CACHE + 64 * (inode_id % 8)`; `read_block` sets `cached_block_id`. Neither `write_*` updates them.
- `superblock->used_inode_num` / `used_block_num` must be maintained by `alloc_*`/`free_*` — `do_statfs` reads them straight out.

Struct offsets (compiled and verified): `sizeof(superblock_t)=512`, `sizeof(inode_t)=64`, `sizeof(dir_entry_t)=32`, `sizeof(dir_t)=4096`, `sizeof(fd_t)=24`. `dir_entry_t`: `type@0`, `name@1..29`, `inode@30`. `inode_t`: `mode@0, owner@4, size@8, direct_blocks@12, indirect_blocks@52, link@60`. `fd_t`: `inode@0, access@2, rd_pos@8, wr_pos@16`.

### 3b. Output formats

**`statfs` — fully fixed by shipped code, zero freedom.** `kernel/fs/fs.c:43-51`:
```c
prints("used inode: %d/%d\n", superblock->used_inode_num, superblock->inode_num);
prints("used block: %d/%d\n", superblock->used_block_num, superblock->block_num);
*print_location_y = *print_location_y + 2;
```
Two lines, e.g. `used inode: 1/4096` / `used block: 1/262144`. The shell prints nothing itself and does not bump `print_location_y` (`test_shell.c:351-358`).

**`mkfs` — the count is fixed, the text is not.** `fs.c:36-38` does `mkfs(1); … *print_location_y += 11;`. So **`mkfs(1)` must print exactly 11 `'\n'`-terminated lines**, and `mkfs(0)` must print **zero** (it is called at `init/main.c:245`, before `init_screen()` at :254). Return non-zero iff it actually formatted — `main()` branches on it for "File System Initialized Successfully" vs "No Need to Initialize File System", and `do_mkfs` returns 0 early when `superblock->magic == MAGIC` without calling `mkfs`. Note `mkfs(0)` must `read_superblock()` and check the magic itself; `do_mkfs` reads it first, but `main()` does not.

**`ls` — the format is implementer-defined; only the contract is fixed.** `test_shell.c:414-452`:
- `ls` → `sys_ls("\0", 0, &print_location_y)`, **return value ignored**.
- `ls -k` → never reaches `do_ls`; goes to `sys_show_exec`, whose house style is `prints("%s    ", name)` for all entries then `prints("\n")`, `+1` (`sched.c:238-247`). Matching that for `mode == 0` is the obvious choice.
- `ls -al [path]` → `sys_ls(argv[2], 1, …)`; with `argc == 2`, `argv[2]` is first set to `""`.
- `ls path` → `sys_ls(argv[1], 0, …)`.
- **Return 0 ⇒ the shell prints `No Such dir!` and bumps y by 1.** Non-zero = success.
- `dirname == ""` means the current directory (`current_dir_inode` / `current_dir_block`).
- `*print_location_y` += exactly the number of `'\n'` emitted (§2d), under `enable_sum()/disable_sum()` since it is a user pointer.
- `mode == 1` is the detailed listing; README (`README.md:43`) says only "打印详细信息". Fields available to show: `dir_entry_t.type`, `inode_t.size`, `inode_t.link`, and the inode id. Keep it ≤ ~34 lines (§2b) and each `prints()` call < 256 bytes (§2l).

**`cat`** — no format constraints, but: fill the caller's 1121-byte buffer, NUL-terminate always (including on failure — set `buffer[0] = '\0'`), keep lines under 80 chars (§2c), return value ignored, and copy only the file's **first sector** per `README.md:45`.

**The four boolean commands** — non-zero = success, 0 = failure, shell prints and bumps y by 1 either way:
| syscall | success | failure | shell line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `do_mkdir` | `make dir %s successfully` | `make dir %s failed` | 374-385 |
| `do_rmdir` | `remove dir %s successfully` | `remove dir %s failed` | 401-412 |
| `do_cd` | `cd dir %s successfully` | `cd dir %s failed` | 467-478 |
| `do_touch` | `create file %s successfully` | `create file %s failed` | 494-505 |
| `do_link` | `create link file %s successfully` | `failed to create link file %s` | 565-577 |

`do_link(filename, newfile, mode)` is called as `sys_link(argv[1 + mode], argv[2 + mode], mode)` (`test_shell.c:567`) with `mode = 1` iff `argv[1]` is `-s` (`:556-559`). Per `README.md:43`: hard link (`mode 0`) reuses the target's i-node and bumps `inode->link`; soft link (`mode 1`) gets **its own i-node but shares the target's blocks** — deliberately unlike Linux.

**`do_fopen` must return a raw index into `fd_list[0..9]`** — pinned by the shipped `do_fclose` (`file.c:40-43`): `fd_list[fd].access = O_EMPTY;`, no translation, no bounds check.

### 3c. Path-resolution rule (`README.md:43`)
`mkdir` / `rmdir` resolve to the **second-to-last** component and operate on the parent; `ls` / `cd` resolve to the **last** component, which must be a directory. `do_touch` (`README.md:45`) resolves the directory, `alloc_inode()`s, then modifies the second-to-last directory.
